Lamingtons (makes 16)
Sponge: 4 eggs, 3/4 cup caster sugar, 1 cup self-raising flour, 2 tbsp cornflour, 1 tbsp melted butter
Icing: 3 cups icing sugar, 1/3 cup cocoa, 15 g butter, 1/2 cup boiling water
2 cups desiccated coconut
Bake the sponge at 180°C for 20–25 min in a 20 x 30 cm tin. Cool overnight, cut into 16 squares, dip in icing, then roll in coconut.

Anzac biscuits (makes about 24)
1 cup rolled oats
1 cup plain flour
1 cup brown sugar
3/4 cup desiccated coconut
125 g butter
2 tbsp golden syrup
1/2 tsp bicarb soda dissolved in 2 tbsp boiling water
Oven 160°C fan-forced. Roll into balls, flatten slightly and bake for 12–15 minutes until golden.

Grandma Joan's pavlova
6 egg whites at room temperature
1 1/2 cups caster sugar
2 tsp cornflour
1 tsp white vinegar
1 tsp vanilla
300 ml thickened cream, whipped
Pulp of 4 passionfruit, 250 g strawberries
Beat the whites to soft peaks, add the sugar a spoonful at a time, then fold in the cornflour, vinegar and vanilla. Bake at 120°C for 1 1/2 hours, then cool in the oven with the door ajar.

Campfire damper (serves 6)
3 cups self-raising flour
1 tsp salt
90 g butter, chilled and cubed
1 1/4 cups milk
Rub the butter into the flour and salt, then stir in the milk to form a soft dough. Shape into a round, score a cross on top and bake at 200°C for 25–30 min, or in a camp oven over coals. Serve with golden syrup.

Roast pumpkin soup – serves 4
1.2 kg butternut pumpkin, peeled and cubed
1 brown onion, chopped
2 garlic cloves
1 L chicken or vegetable stock
1/2 cup cream, plus extra to serve
Roast the pumpkin at 200°C for 30 min. Soften the onion and garlic, add the pumpkin and stock, simmer for 15 min and blend until smooth. Season and stir through the cream.
Prep 15 min · Cook 50 min · approx. 285 kcal per serve

4 barramundi fillets (about 180 g each)
2 tbsp olive oil
1 tsp ground lemon myrtle
Zest and juice of 1 lemon

Chapter 4
The Railway Comes to Merrigal Park
When the line from the city finally reached Merrigal Park in March 1912, the township had just 340 residents, a general store and two hotels. Within a decade the population had grown to more than 1,800, and the paddocks east of the station were divided into quarter-acre blocks that sold for £45 each.
The original timber station burned down in 1937 and was replaced by the brick building that still stands on Platform 1.

Staying safe in hot weather
On days above 35°C, drink 2 to 3 litres of water even if you do not feel thirsty, and avoid alcohol and hot or sugary drinks.
Check on elderly neighbours and people living alone at least twice a day.
Never leave children or pets in a parked car. On a 30°C day the temperature inside a car can reach 60°C within 15 minutes.
If someone becomes confused or stops sweating, call 000 immediately.

Growing tomatoes in a temperate climate
Sow seed indoors in late August, about 6 mm deep, and keep the punnets at 20–25°C until they germinate, usually in 7 to 10 days. Plant out after the last frost, spacing plants 50–60 cm apart in full sun.
Feed every 2 weeks with a liquid fertiliser high in potassium once the first flowers appear. Water deeply at the base 2 or 3 times a week rather than a little every day, which encourages shallow roots.

Superb Fairy-wren (Malurus cyaneus)
Length 14 cm; weight about 10 g. The breeding male has a bright blue crown and ear patches with a black throat, while females and young birds are brown with a reddish-orange patch around the bill and eye.
Groups of 2 to 8 birds defend a territory of 1 to 4 hectares all year. Females lay 3 or 4 eggs and may raise up to 3 broods in a season.
Common in gardens with dense, low shrubs across south-eastern Australia.

Kurrawong Heritage Walk
Allow about 90 minutes for the full 3.2 km loop, which starts at the Visitor Centre on Main St.
Stop 1: The Courthouse (1884). Built of local bluestone at a cost of £2,600, it heard its last case in 1971.
Stop 2: Kurrawong Bakery, baking on this site since 1903.
Stop 3: The Federation Hotel. Look for the original iron lace on the first-floor verandah.
The walk is mostly flat and suitable for prams and wheelchairs.

Caring for your new puppy
Puppies need 4 meals a day until 12 weeks of age, then 3 meals a day until 6 months.
Vaccinations are given at 6–8 weeks, 10–12 weeks and 14–16 weeks. Do not walk your puppy in public places until 2 weeks after the final vaccination.
Start heartworm prevention by 12 weeks. Worm every 2 weeks until 12 weeks old, then monthly until 6 months.
